statement: Online surveys can no longer be trusted unless researchers confirm that respondents are real people.
AI can help code qualitative data, but humans should still make the final interpretation.
Researchers should always disclose when AI was used to collect or generate data.
AI-simulated participants can replace real people in early-stage or low-stakes research.
AI-simulated participants flatten and stereotype identity groups, so they should never stand in for minority voices.
Testing AI's influence on real people without their consent is justified if the findings help society.
People are more honest with an AI interviewer than with a human one.
How closely should synthetic responses match real human responses to be useful? Is an 80% match enough to consider them representative?
